writeup.headline: Fortinet rates Buy on strong growth, quality and momentum, held back by a high valuation.
writeup.thesis: Fortinet scores 71, a Buy, driven by top-tier quality (80.2% gross margin, 32.4% operating margin, 41.4% FCF margin, diluted share count down 4.2% year on year) and a net-cash balance sheet that scores 100. Growth is strong and improving, with latest-quarter revenue growth of 25.6% year on year, TTM revenue growth of 18.8%, and growth sped up by 5.5 pp from the previous quarter. The shares have strong momentum: they are up 106.1% from 12 months ago to 1 month ago and the price is 5.0% below its 52-week high. News is mildly positive after a Q3 beat and a raised 2026 revenue and billings guidance. Valuation is the main drag at a score of 16. In absolute terms the multiples are high, at 18.0x sales, 43.5x FCF and 54.1x EV/EBIT, with FCF yield 2.7 pp below the 10-year Treasury yield. The stock is also expensive against its own history.
key_risks: High absolute valuation (18.0x sales, 54.1x EV/EBIT) leaves little room for a growth slowdown.
The P/S multiple is more expensive than at 58 of the last 61 month-ends, so the shares could fall back if the multiple returns toward its usual level.
After a sharp run, with the price 45.3% above its 200-day average, the shares could pull back hard.
A new patent suit over core FortiGate and FortiOS products, and a pending securities class action.
Mixed analyst views: consensus is still Hold, with Arete at Sell and JPMorgan at Underweight.
what_would_change: Up to Strong Buy (9 points needed): a lower valuation, through a price pullback or faster earnings growth, or continued growth acceleration.
Down to Hold (7 points of cushion): a fading trend score if momentum reverses, or slowing revenue growth.
Adverse litigation developments or a guidance cut would weigh on the news risk score.
